scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API with Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum both true. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader at term 1 in configuration {1,2,3}; a remove-3 ConfChange is proposed on the leader and applied on every node; node 3 is then re-added by a committed ConfChange with leader 1 unchanged; the logical clock is advanced ten rounds with delivery between rounds; then Node.Propose is invoked on the re-added node 3 with a 1200 ms context and a 900 ms observation window, followed by a control invocation on never-removed node 2. Events record returned values, errors, elapsed times, membership, leader and payload presence.
assumptions: Ticks are delivered in ten rounds with delivery between rounds so heartbeats keep the followers' election timers reset while both timeouts advance.
CheckQuorum's activity tracking is therefore exercised (the leader keeps quorum) and PreVote's pre-election phase is available, but no election is triggered during the observation.
excluded: Message loss, partitions and leader changes
RawNode paths and async storage writes

basis.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} and with PreVote and CheckQuorum enabled. Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose a remove-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's own configuration excludes it; propose an add-3 ConfChange and wait until node 3 is a voter again with leader still 1. Advance the clock ten rounds with delivery between rounds and record the resulting context (leader, leader state, membership). Invoke Node.Propose on node 3 with a 1200 ms context, observe for 900 ms, and record the result and whether its payload is committed anywhere. Then invoke Node.Propose on node 2 and record its result and committed payload.
basis.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface under the recommended configuration: a proposal from a re-added voter with a healthy known leader must reach a decision or return an error rather than staying pending, while proposals from other members must continue to complete.

comparisons.description: Under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the clock running, the re-added voter's invocation did not return inside the window.
Its payload was not committed anywhere.
Control: the never-removed member's invocation under the same flags returned.
Control: its payload was committed on all nodes, so the group was healthy under those flags.

before.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader in the initial configuration {1,2,3} supplied by the storage ConfState; committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes are proposed on the leader and applied on every node. Then the experiment issues, on re-added node 3: the witness invocation (2500 ms context), an invocation with a context that never expires (observed for 2000 ms), and two retry attempts (900 ms contexts) each paired with a proposal by never-removed node 2 committed in the same interval; it also runs the control on node 2, then forces a leader change to node 2 at term 2 and issues a further invocation on node 3, and finally observes whether the context-free invocation was admitted by the re-armed gate and whether its payload committed. Every invocation records whether it returned, the error, elapsed time, the node's observed voter status and leader, and whether the payload reached any node's committed entries.
assumptions: Message delivery between the three in-process nodes is reliable and ordered per sender; no ticks are delivered, so leader 1 stays stable until the experiment forces the leader change.
Storage appends of Ready.Entries happen before the Ready's messages are dispatched.

The removal and re-addition are the committed conf changes the driver applies; node 3 applies both through Node.ApplyConfChange. The context-free invocation is issued before any leader change and is not cancelled by the harness, so its admission can only come from the run loop re-arming its receive side.
excluded: RawNode.Propose (no gate exists on that path)
Network faults: delivery is reliable, so non-delivery cannot be attributed to message loss
Node stop as a release path for the context-free invocation (the harness no longer stops the node mid-scenario)

prefix.before: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3} (captured test helper withPeers). Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node then reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose on node 1 a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointImplicit carrying the single change remove node 3, so the configuration becomes joint and raft itself proposes the entry that leaves the joint state; wait until node 3 has applied the conf-change entry carrying the removal and its configuration excludes it from both halves (voter=false, outgoing=false), recording that transition as removal_applied. Then propose an add-3 ConfChange on node 1 and wait until node 3's applied entries contain it and node 3's configuration includes node 3 again (voter=true) with leader still 1. Then run the witness invocation, the context-free invocation (through ten rounds of ticks to every node with delivery in between), the configuration proposal, the control, the two retry/progress intervals, and the forced leader change with the final invocation and the post-re-arm observations on node 3.

responsibility.before: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface: a Propose invocation on a voting member whose leader is known must either reach a proposal outcome (appended locally or forwarded to the leader) or return an error to the caller, within an interval the caller can bound; a context-free invocation must not be silently held until an unrelated leadership change admits it.
responsibility.after: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface under the recommended configuration: a proposal from a re-added voter with a healthy known leader must reach a decision or return an error rather than staying pending, while proposals from other members must continue to complete.

before.description: The invocation on the re-added voter did not return inside the observation window although that node's own configuration lists it as a voter.
The pending invocation ended only when the caller's own context deadline expired; raft produced no proposal outcome.
The re-added voter's payload never appeared in any node's committed entries within the window.
With a context that never expires, the invocation was still pending after the observation window while leader 1 stayed stable.
The context-free invocation's payload was not committed during that window.
The still-pending context-free invocation was admitted once the leader change re-armed the gate.
The admitted context-free invocation's payload was committed afterwards.
After ten rounds of ticks to every node the context-free invocation was still pending, with leader 1 unchanged and the node still a voter, so the running logical clock did not itself release it.
A configuration change proposed through the re-added voter did not return inside the window while leader 1 was stable.
No node applied the configuration change proposed through the re-added voter.
Control: the never-removed member's invocation on the same leader returned immediately.
Control: the never-removed member's payload was committed, so the leader and proposal path were healthy.
First retry on the re-added voter did not return while leader 1 was still stable.
Second retry on the re-added voter did not return while leader 1 was still stable.
During the first retry interval the cluster committed a proposal made by the never-removed member.
During the second retry interval the cluster committed a proposal made by the never-removed member.
After the forced leader change a new invocation on node 3 returned immediately.
After the forced leader change that invocation's payload was committed.

revision_reason: Configuration and observation change: the witness scenario now runs with Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum enabled, the logical clock is advanced ten rounds with delivery between rounds before the witness invocation, and the witness and control events are emitted under their own names (checked_removal_proposed, checked_removal_applied, checked_context, checked_invocation, checked_result, checked_commit, checked_control_invocation, checked_control_result, checked_control_commit) with a 1200 ms context and a 900 ms window. The removal and re-addition are simple ConfChanges applied on every node, and four comparisons cover the pending witness invocation, its absent payload, and the control that returns and commits.
